_comment: Aelgard Sootworks bestiary. The industrial forge-smog region — iron dragons, foreman wights, rust elementals, clockwork abominations. Tone: short, soot-mouthed, tool-noun-heavy. Threats are machines that kept working after their operators died.
_region_tone: furnace roar, oily black grit on every surface, quotas printed on the wall. A thing that moves here is either a tool or about to be scrap.

monsters.name: Cinder golem
bible: A cinder golem coalesces from a dead foreman's ash-pile — particularly if that foreman died angry at his crew. It inherits the foreman's bellow, the foreman's walking gait, and a perfect memory of who was slacking.
They patrol the smelt-floor where they died, shouting names that mostly no longer apply. Younger workers joke about it. Older workers join the shout; the golem is ignored but never contradicted.
Killing a cinder golem fully extinguishes the bellow. The silence makes the night-shift slow for a week.
monsters.anti_pattern_note: every cinder golem has a NAME inherited from its foreman — encounters should reveal that name somehow.

monsters.name: Iron dragon
monsters.examine: A dragon made of iron. Immune to melee without dragonfire protection.
bible: The Sootworks ironworks bred iron dragons the way a granary breeds rats — as an unplanned consequence of long proximity. Broken iron, melted and remelted a thousand times in the same pit, eventually takes on opinions. The opinion is: be a dragon.
They are slower than their organic cousins but hit harder and cannot be melted by their own dragonfire. A smith's hammer will not mark them. A warhammer might.
Sootworks management accepts iron dragons as an unavoidable overhead and has a standing order to bury dead ones at least a mile from any forge, to prevent heredity.
monsters.habitat: deep Sootworks pits, ironworks caverns, the Blast Hollow
monsters.reagent_callout: Drops Draconic visage shard (1/2048) — reagent for the Sootworks anti-dragon shield upgrade.

monsters.name: Steel dragon
monsters.examine: A dragon made of steel. Even tougher than iron.
bible: A steel dragon is what an iron dragon becomes after a generation of living adjacent to the Sootworks steel furnaces. The alloy has gained the dragon's bulk but not lost the iron dragon's irritability.

Their hide is layered — the outer plate is steel, the muscle-band beneath is wrought iron, the core is cast. Piercing through all three layers takes a specific tactic; magical energy disrupts the metallurgy.
The last head-of-Sootworks to try taming one is a plaque on the Hollow's southern wall. The plaque is short.
monsters.habitat: Steel Hollow below the main Sootworks, the secondary forges at night
monsters.reagent_callout: Drops Draconic visage (1/5000) — reagent for the Anti-dragon shield endgame upgrade.

monsters.name: Forge wraith
bible: A forge wraith is the superheated air above a forge that has burned continuously for forty years without rest. When the forge finally cools, the air does not want to. It retains the shape of the forge mouth, the heat of working temperature, and the stubbornness of the smith who kept it lit.
Wraiths do not leave the building they formed in. They pursue a target to the edge of the doorway and stop, always within an arm's length of crossing.
Killing one requires rapid, concussive damage — the heat-shape can outrun any cutting edge but cannot reassemble from shattered halves.
monsters.habitat: forge-houses whose fires have died, the abandoned Southrun workshops
monsters.anti_pattern_note: door-threshold mechanic is core — do NOT let the wraith follow outside. The bait-out-and-shut is explicit in the encounter script.

monsters.name: Clockwork abomination
monsters.examine: Three clocks for a head. None of them tell the same time.
bible: Sootworks inventor-apprentices, left unsupervised in the workshops during the night shift, produce constructs that should not work and do. A clockwork abomination is one such construct: a humanoid frame with three clocks for a head, each set by a different apprentice who did not coordinate.
The heads argue. The torso obeys the most recent shout, which is whichever head is chiming. It is therefore confused most of the time but ferocious when any head strikes the hour.
A winding-key stop from a combatant can briefly silence one clock. Silence all three and the frame collapses.
monsters.habitat: Sootworks apprentice workshops, the condemned east wing
monsters.reagent_callout: Drops clockwork spring (reagent for tick-wound crossbow) and a winding key (slayer-niche tool vs construct-tag).

monsters.name: Dust devil
monsters.examine: A whirlwind of coal dust. Smells like cough.
bible: Sootworks air is thick with particulates from decades of incomplete combustion. On bad days — which are most days — the dust organises itself into a column three feet wide and eight feet tall, with approximately murderous intent.
A dust devil is not a ghost; it is a local weather. It can be dispelled by a strong mechanical fan or by a well-placed magical wind, but the underlying dust-count makes re-formation inevitable.
Sootworks foremen grudgingly issue face-masks for dust-devil-prone zones. The masks are older than some foremen.
monsters.habitat: Sootworks blast-corridors, coal-dust storage, unventilated pits
monsters.anti_pattern_note: face-mask item (regional reward) suppresses aggro within 3 tiles. Encounter design should not assume uncovered-face player.

monsters.name: Crazed engineer
monsters.examine: Pockets full of schematics for machines that don't work.
bible: Sootworks engineers are a specific archetype — twenty years of trade-training, five years of consistent overwork, and one too many failed commissions. A crazed engineer has entered the final phase, where he is building a machine he cannot describe to anyone else but insists will solve the Problem.
He will not attack a fellow engineer; he will attack anyone who touches his schematic pile. The schematic pile is always present and always chaotic.
Killed, he drops a partial blueprint — one sheet of a larger design that may or may not be completable by combining sheets from other crazed engineers scattered across the Sootworks.
monsters.habitat: workshop lofts, abandoned commission sites, coal-bunker interiors
monsters.reagent_callout: Each engineer drops one unique blueprint sheet (1/64) — 12 collectible sheets combine into the Sootworks Automaton (pet follower, not combat).

monsters.name: Furnace imp
monsters.examine: Takes tools. Returns most of them.
bible: Sootworks furnaces are hot enough that small fire-imps nest inside them, undetected for years. When the fire goes out, they come out. They are shoulder-high, coal-coloured, and professionally mischievous.
An imp will take any tool left unattended and return it nine times out of ten, somewhere nearby. The tenth time the tool is gone. The tool is always the most valuable one on the bench.
They do not attack first. If provoked they throw hot slag with uncomfortable aim.
monsters.habitat: cold furnace interiors, tool-bench backs, abandoned coal scuttles
monsters.anti_pattern_note: passive. Attacking an imp provokes ALL imps in line-of-sight.

monsters.name: Rust elemental
monsters.examine: A century of oxidation given a frame.
bible: Where water leaks into a Sootworks iron vault for a century, a rust elemental forms — the body of the slow chemistry made manifest. Its skin is scale-flake; its joints creak; its attack is a contagious oxidation.
Iron weapons degrade in its presence. Mithril weakens. Adamant endures but dulls. Only rune-grade and enchanted blades keep their edge through a full encounter.
A rust elemental cannot be killed by destruction; it can be separated. Spilling its contents across a wide enough area reduces it below critical mass, and the scattered flake is inert.
monsters.habitat: flooded Sootworks vaults, century-rain-wet cellars, the drowned east cellar
monsters.anti_pattern_note: weapon-degradation is durable debuff on iron/mithril gear for 30 minutes. Warn the player.

monsters.name: Slag troll
monsters.examine: A troll made of metallurgical waste. Slow. Heavy. Furious.
bible: Sootworks slag — the molten waste from smelting — is poured into designated pits. If the pit fills and a stray heat-source re-liquefies it, a troll-shaped thing sometimes stands up. It retains the pit's exact chemistry, which is never the same twice.
Slag trolls are slow enough to outpace at walking speed, but they do not tire. They pursue a specific target for days, walking through walls, fences, and lesser structures.
The only reliable containment is a steel cage pre-cast with rune anchors. Sootworks management has three in storage. Two are cracked.
monsters.habitat: slag pits, the East Trench, long-abandoned overflow pools
monsters.reagent_callout: Drops slag-core (1/256) — reagent for the Sootworks endgame crush weapon 'The Overpour'.

monsters.name: Boiler spectre
monsters.examine: The ghost of a boiler-room death.
bible: Boiler accidents are the Sootworks' most common industrial fatality. The men who die in boiler-room explosions often leave spectres — not of themselves, but of the boiler-room moment: the whistle, the flash, the gasp.
A boiler spectre inhabits a specific mechanical room. It does not leave. It attacks anyone in the room, with an attack that is functionally a small reenactment of its death.
The only way to free a spectre is to replace the boiler fully. This is expensive. Most foremen choose containment (lock the door, post a warning) over replacement.
monsters.habitat: Sootworks boiler rooms, specifically rooms with recorded accidents
monsters.anti_pattern_note: encounter constrained to the boiler room. Spectre CANNOT be kited out.

monsters.name: Valve gremlin
monsters.examine: Rides the pipes. Costs you ten minutes per encounter.
bible: Sootworks pipe-gremlins are a low-grade pest endemic to the steam-pipe network. Each one lives inside a specific valve; opening the valve lets the gremlin out. Closing the valve traps it again.
They sabotage pipe-work for sport. A ruined Sootworks production week typically begins with a valve gremlin that nobody reported, out of shame.
They drop a valve fitting that, accumulated, becomes a useful crafting stockpile for plumbing repair professions.
monsters.habitat: steam-pipe junctions, valve-clusters, any long corridor with wall-mounted pressure gauges
monsters.reagent_callout: Steam valve fittings stack — 10 fittings at the Sootworks plumbing bench = one steam-compression flask (consumable mid-combat).

monsters.name: Smog wraith
monsters.examine: A cloud with a face you half-remember.
bible: On the worst air-quality days, Sootworks smog gains definition — a vaguely human shape drifts through the streets. The shape is usually recognisable to somebody; long-term workers swear the wraith has their uncle's face, or a foreman who died years back.
Smog wraiths are attracted to respiration. They will approach an unmasked worker and linger, causing cough-sickness over the hour.
A strong cross-wind disperses them temporarily. The wind goes with the weather; so does the wraith.
monsters.habitat: smog-dense Sootworks corridors, the yellow-alert air days
monsters.anti_pattern_note: mask item (regional reward) provides aggro suppression; smog wraiths are a mask-propaganda mechanic.

region_flavor_drops: Draconic visage (1/5000 from Steel dragon — reagent: Anti-dragon shield upgrade)
Draconic visage shard (1/2048 from Iron dragon — reagent pair with visage)
Slag-core (1/256 from Slag troll — reagent: The Overpour, endgame crush)
Blueprint sheet (12 distinct — collection: Sootworks Automaton pet)
